post.caption: Emerald has a rare red cousin. Red beryl is a rare color of beryl, the emerald mineral, and trace manganese gives it a raspberry red color. Maynard Bixby found it in Utah's Thomas Range in 1904, and the name bixbite was dropped to avoid confusion with bixbyite. Utah's Wah Wah Mountains are the only known commercial source. Reportedly, one red beryl crystal is found per 150,000 diamonds, and most cut stones weigh well under one carat. It is hard, at 7.5 to 8 on the Mohs scale, and the color forms as the crystal grows, not from treatment. It is sometimes called red emerald.
